Question: How many subsets containing three different numbers can be selected from the set \(\{89, 95, 99, 132, 166, 173\}\) so that the sum of the three numbers is even?
Solution:
Only whether each number is odd or even matters. The odd numbers are \(89,95,99,173\), and the even numbers are \(132,166\).

A sum of three integers is even exactly when it contains zero or two odd numbers. Zero odd numbers would require three even numbers, but only two are available. Thus every valid subset contains two odd numbers and one even number.

Count the odd pairs by their smaller member. If the smaller member is \(89\), there are three possible partners; if it is \(95\), there are two; if it is \(99\), there is one. This counts each pair once, giving \(3+2+1=6\) pairs. Each pair can be joined with either even number, so the number of subsets is
\[
6\times2=12.
\]
Every valid subset has exactly one such odd pair and one even number, so none are omitted or counted twice. The answer is \(12\), choice D.
